rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Monera holds the prokaryotes: bacteria are unicellular cells of 0.5–5 µm with a peptidoglycan wall, 70S ribosomes, a naked circular nucleoid plus plasmids, and no membrane-bound organelles; they take coccus, bacillus, spirillum and vibrio shapes, divide by binary fission in about twenty minutes, and grow through lag, log, stationary and decline phases.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Shapes: coccus, bacillus, spirillum, vibrio.
Growth: lag, log, stationary, death.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Nucleoid vs nucleus:** the nucleoid is an unenclosed DNA region; a nucleus has a double membrane — bacteria have the former only.  ·  **Heterocyst vs vegetative cell:** heterocyst = thick-walled nitrogen-fixing cell without oxygenic photosynthesis; vegetative cells photosynthesise.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Mycoplasma has no wall. It is the exception, not the diagram.  ·  Do not draw mitochondria inside a bacterium.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Lactobacillus*** — milk → curd.  ·  ***Rhizobium*** — legume nodule nitrogen fixation.

rows.label: Limitation

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Label five parts of a bacterial cell.  ·  Match Rhizobium, Nostoc and Lactobacillus to a role.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "Gram+ = violet = thick wall; Gram− = pink = LPS shield."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Q.** What are plasmids? **Answer.** Small, **circular, self-replicating accessory DNA molecules** in bacteria, separate from the nucleoid chromosome. It survives boiling, drying, disinfectants and even years of waiting, and **germinates** back into a vegetative cell when conditions improve — the reason autoclaving, not mere boiling,…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Prokaryote = pre-nucleus:** all defining Monera features (size, ribosomes, wall, replication speed) follow from lacking a nuclear envelope and organelles.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Monera: prokaryotes — no nuclear envelope, 70S ribosomes, peptidoglycan wall, circular DNA + plasmids, binary fission in 20–30 min.  ·  Shapes: coccus (diplo/strepto/staphylo), bacillus, spirillum, vibrio. Gram-positive violet/thick peptidoglycan; Gram-negative pink/thin + LPS.  ·  Nutrition: photoautotrophic (cyanobacteria), chemoautotrophic (Nitrosomonas, Nitrobacter), saprophytic, parasitic, symbiotic (Rhizobium, E. coli).  ·  Growth curve: lag → log → stationary → decline.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Bacteria were the only life forms for roughly the first 2 billion years of Earth's history.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: ***Nitrosomonas/Nitrobacter*** — nitrification steps of the nitrogen cycle.  ·  ***Anabaena azollae*** — symbiont of Azolla; rice biofertiliser.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Bacterial ribosomes are → B  ·  A heterocyst is used for → B

rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Life at Its Simplest and Most Successful Monera is the kingdom of **prokaryotes** — organisms whose genetic material is not enclosed in a nucleus. rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Cyanobacteria: chlorophyll a + phycocyanin, heterocysts fix N2 with nitrogenase (Anabaena in Azolla for rice).  ·  **Pili vs flagella:** pili are attachment/conjugation hairs; flagella are rotary motility organelles.  ·  **Mesosome vs mitochondrion:** mesosome = plasma-membrane infolding in bacteria; mitochondrion = eukaryotic organelle absent in prokaryotes.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ***Bacillus/Clostridium*** — endospore formers; survive boiling.  ·  The bacteria characteristics question repeated in 2023 and 2024 — always attach named beneficial and harmful examples.  ·  "In the twentieth minute, one bacterium becomes two — and the exponential world begins."

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Why does penicillin kill bacteria but not human cells? **Answer.** Penicillin blocks the enzymes that **cross-link peptidoglycan**, the polymer unique to the bacterial cell wall.
